text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.7% today as oil prices climbed sharply, with US crude jumping to $103.37 per barrel (up from around $100 earlier this week). The bigger driver appears to be geopolitical: Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran aimed at de-escalating US-Iran tensions, which reduces the risk of supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil. When that risk eases, it typically pushes prices lower initially, but the mere fact of negotiation and continued tanker traffic through the strait suggests the market is pricing in stabilization rather than escalation, which supports prices and refiner margins.

The company also benefits from the broader energy environment: refining earnings have surged as fuel supplies tightened, and with the wide gap between world oil ($123) and US oil ($103), refiners with access to global markets are capturing extra margin. Over the past two weeks the stock has climbed 5%, riding both crude strength and the tailwind of high refining profitability even as President Trump criticizes oil industry profits.
